ip_top_stories.title: Eleonora Rosati, lawyer: 'Artists are already thinking about how to protect themselves from AI; Taylor Swift has registered her voice'
ip_top_stories.summary: IP lawyer Eleonora Rosati discusses how artists including Taylor Swift are proactively seeking legal protections against AI, including voice registration. The interview covers emerging strategies for protecting personality rights and creative works in the face of generative AI. This connects to a broader trend of celebrities pursuing novel legal avenues against AI misuse.

ip_top_stories.title: California Senate votes to advance AI Copyright bill
ip_top_stories.summary: The California Senate has voted to advance a bill addressing AI copyright, marking a significant legislative development in the United States. The bill's progress signals growing momentum for state-level regulatory action on AI and intellectual property. This follows ongoing federal debates about how copyright law should apply to AI-generated and AI-trained content.

ip_top_stories.title: News Orgs Must Give Cohere AI Use Policies
ip_top_stories.summary: A ruling or regulatory development requires news organisations to provide Cohere with their AI use policies, raising questions about how publishers engage with AI companies over content licensing and usage rights. The story touches on the intersection of media licensing and AI training data obligations. It represents a notable development for publishers navigating AI company relationships.

ip_top_stories.title: Big Tech Is a Thief and Liar, Says NYT Publisher
ip_top_stories.summary: The publisher of The New York Times has publicly accused Big Tech companies of theft and dishonesty in relation to the use of journalistic content for AI training. The statement reflects escalating tensions between major news publishers and AI developers over unauthorised use of copyrighted material. It adds to growing industry pressure for enforceable licensing frameworks.

ip_top_stories.title: AI Deepfake Law NO FAKES Act Advances in Congress With Key Senate Committee Vote
ip_top_stories.summary: The NO FAKES Act, US federal legislation targeting AI-generated deepfakes, has advanced following a key Senate committee vote. The bill would create new protections for individuals' voices and likenesses against unauthorised AI replication. Its progress represents a significant step towards federal regulation of AI and personality rights.

ip_further_links.title: How US courts are addressing fair use questions in AI training and copyright disputes
ip_further_links.summary: An overview of how US courts are currently handling fair use arguments in cases involving AI training data and copyright infringement.

ip_further_links.title: Rights holders and generative AI companies: infringement risks meet competition pressure
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of the tensions between rights holders and generative AI companies, examining how infringement risks intersect with competitive dynamics in the AI industry.

ip_further_links.title: APRA AMCOS Reveals Australian And New Zealand Songs Found In AI Training Datasets
ip_further_links.summary: Australian and New Zealand music rights body APRA AMCOS has disclosed that songs from its members were found in AI training datasets, raising fresh concerns about unlicensed use of musical works.

ip_further_links.title: Charity Advising Canberra on AI Copyright Laws Funded by Anthropic-Linked Donors
ip_further_links.summary: A charity advising the Australian government on AI copyright legislation has received funding from donors linked to AI company Anthropic, raising questions about potential conflicts of interest in policy formation.

ip_further_links.title: Bombay High Court allows Preity Zinta to sue online platforms for infringement of content produced with AI
ip_further_links.summary: The Bombay High Court has granted Bollywood actress Preity Zinta permission to pursue legal action against Google and Meta over AI-generated deepfakes and unauthorised use of her likeness.

ip_further_links.title: The novel legal strategy that Taylor Swift, Matthew McConaughey are using to fight AI - Straight Arrow News
ip_further_links.summary: Taylor Swift, Matthew McConaughey and other public figures are reportedly using a novel legal strategy — including voice and likeness registration — to protect themselves against AI-generated misuse.

ip_further_links.title: Bigger verdicts, fewer injunctions: AI, telecoms, and trade secrets shake up litigation
ip_further_links.summary: A report examines shifting litigation trends including larger damages verdicts and fewer injunctions in cases involving AI, telecoms, and trade secrets.

ip_further_links.title: AI.Law sues competitor Eve Legal for alleged patent infringement
ip_further_links.summary: Legal AI firm AI.Law has filed a patent infringement lawsuit against competitor Eve Legal and Butler Labs, marking an early instance of AI-focused legal services companies litigating over intellectual property.

ip_further_links.title: EU Parliament rejects last-minute patent amendments and passes NGT Regulation
ip_further_links.summary: The EU Parliament has rejected late-stage patent-related amendments and passed the New Genomic Techniques Regulation, with IP implications for the biotech sector.

ip_further_links.title: Invisible AI Patent Risks Your Legal Team Is Probably Missing
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis warns that many legal teams are overlooking significant patent risks arising from the deployment of AI tools within organisations.
